user: And I still have time to file, right?
answer:
Based on today's date in our system (15 September 2026), TX-0401 is 57 days old. Whether you can still file depends on the reason code:

| Reason code | Window | Deadline for TX-0401 | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Duplicate charge | 60 days | 18 Sep 2026 | **Open, about 3 days left** |
| Unauthorized debit | 56 days | 14 Sep 2026 | **Closed** |
| Goods not received | 90 days | 18 Oct 2026 | Open |
| Service not rendered | 90 days | 18 Oct 2026 | Open |
| Card-not-present fraud | 120 days | 17 Nov 2026 | Open |

If this is a duplicate charge, you need to act within the next few days. Unauthorized debit is no longer available for this transaction.

Which situation applies to TX-0401? Once you choose, I'll run the eligibility check and confirm the details with you before anything is filed.

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each reason code has a window in days from the transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Customer security policy
## Card blocking
A customer may block a card immediately. Blocking is reversible for 30 days;
after that a replacement card must be ordered.

Glossary
## Chargeback window
The number of days, counted from the transaction date, during which a dispute
may be raised under a given reason code.

Limit operations
## Window definition
Limits are tracked on calendar days, not business days. The daily window runs
from 00:00 to 23:59 CET.
